newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY ENERGY RISE HURTS MVM, NOT MOL - OFFICIAL.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY ENERGY RISE HURTS MVM, NOT MOL - OFFICIAL.

text.p: The Hungarian Energy Office (MEH) said on Friday that the government decision to offer state-owned energy companies lower 1997 profit margins affects the Hungarian Electricity Works (MVM) and the Paks Nuclear Power Station, but not the oil and gas company MOL .
The government decided on Thursday to raise gas prices by 18.8 percent and electricity prices by 24.9 percent from January 1, to assure an eight percent profit margin for the energy sector.

The government also decided that only privatised companies would receive the eight percent margin, and state-owned companies would only get four percent, government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday.
However, Kiss did not specify if the partially privatised MOL would receive eight or four percent.
A MEH official told Reuters on Friday that MOL was not affected by the government's decision to offer lower margins to state-owned companies.
"(The four percent margin) affects MVM and the Paks Nuclear Power Station," said MEH deputy director Gyorgy Bekes.
MOL officials were not immediately available for comment.
A London-based analyst said MOL, as a gas supplier, had good chances to take up most of the money to be generated for gas companies by the energy price rice.
"I think it's justified to say that MOL would take up five-sixth of the price rise, or 15.5 to 16 percent (of the 18.8)," said Gabor Sitanyi of ING Barings.
